speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe where you see the double vision, and does your double vision get worse when you look toward one side? Additionally, have you noticed any slurred speech or difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of fluctuating weakness and vertical diplopia is highly concerning; have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty keeping them open? REQUEST TEST: Anti-AChR antibody, MuSK antibody; REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain, Neck.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Anti-AChR antibody: Present (elevated); MuSK antibody: Not detected; MRI Brain: No acute abnormalities or masses detected; MRI Neck: No thymoma or masses detected.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of vertical diplopia that worsens with upgaze, fluctuating weakness relieved by rest, and symmetric limb involvement is classic for this condition, confirmed by your request for antibody testing and imaging.
